name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 17 points, among the strongest GOP seats
Palmer is an entrenched incumbent who raised roughly $1.05 million; Mercer raised about $6,500 with under $2,000 on hand
No public polls or expert ratings; prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3 percent chance
Outside spending favors Palmer with none opposing him
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Palmer's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial edge over a barely funded challenger make this a foregone conclusion, and markets price a Democratic win at just 3 percent. With no polls or ratings suggesting any vulnerability, the expected margin sits near 20 points Republican.
model.watch: Only a dramatic national wave against Republicans or an unexpected scandal involving Palmer could put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 6th District, anchored in Birmingham's suburbs, leans Republican by about 17 points, and Gary Palmer has held the seat for Republicans since 2015. He is running again and has raised roughly $1.05 million, with outside groups adding support and none spending against him. Democrat Maurice Mercer has raised about $6,500 and reports under $2,000 on hand, leaving him little capacity to compete.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 3 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong partisan lean, Palmer's incumbency and financial advantage, and a favorable environment for Republicans points to a comfortable double-digit Republican win in a race drawing little outside attention.
